title: Edge selection preserves the induced partition
statement: Let $n \in \bbn$, let $\mathit{uf} : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbn$ be a union-find state, and let $\mathit{es}$ be a list of weighted edges over $n$ vertices. Merging into $\mathit{uf}$ only the edges retained by the edge-selection sweep (running the sweep from $\mathit{uf}$ with an empty accumulator) yields a union-find state inducing the same equivalence relation on nodes as merging all of $\mathit{es}$ into $\mathit{uf}$: for all $i, j : \mathrm{Fin}\,n$, the two nodes share a representative after the first process exactly when they share a representative after the second.
hypotheses_covered: uf a union-find state on n nodes
es a list of weighted edges over n vertices
replaced:
Merging the edges selected by the greedy loop into $uf$ gives the same partition as
merging all the input edges into $uf$: the discarded edges never change connectivity.
